newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Korean Air to move to new Kimpo headquarters.
newsitem.headline: Korean Air to move to new Kimpo headquarters.

text.p: Most of Korean Air's (KAL) 8,000 workers in Seoul will be in one building for the first time when the airline officially opens its new 'Airbase' at the capital's Kimpo airport, airline spokesman Muchol Shin has told Reuters.
Many of the staff began moving into their new headquarters last month in preparation for the official opening by KAL president Yang Ho Cho on May 28.
KAL expects operational efficiencies with the new building. Up to now KAL's staff have been housed in separate buildings scattered across the airport site, he said.

The US$250 million, seven storey high KAL Kimpo Operation Centre is dominated by an aircraft maintenance hangar able to accomodate two Boeing 747s and one Airbus wide-bodied aircraft at the same time.
The new building's eye-catching steel roof weighing 4,600 tonnes was hoisted into position in a complicated series of mnnoeuvres and is supported by just three columns, Shin said.
